headline: Elon Musk agreed with a post saying the world will soon run on code nobody has read, adding that software will become machine code rather than lines of code.
score_reason: A forecast by one famous person in a social-media reply; plausible direction, no evidence, and the article itself cites mixed job data.
importance_line: Software developers, especially beginners, are most affected, but it is one man's forecast in a social media reply, and the article's own job data is mixed.
summary: India Today reports that Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX and Tesla, replied "100 percent" to an X user who wrote that soon the world will run on code nobody has read, adding, "There won't be lines of software as we know them, just machine code." The article notes software job postings in the US rose nearly 15% since February 2025 per Indeed Hiring Lab data cited by CNBC, while employment of 22 to 25 year-olds in AI-exposed fields has fallen 16%, per Stanford's 2026 AI Index.
notes: Full text read (India Today's AMP page; repeated text ignored). The jobs figures come from Indeed and Stanford as cited by India Today; the Stanford note says AI alone is not shown to have caused the decline. 'SpaceX and Tesla' title is general knowledge, not in the article.
